items.headline: Iranian crude exports collapse under the Hormuz blockade as oil and global yields rise again
items.category: Geopolitics / Energy / Macro / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Reuters reports that meaningful Iranian crude exports through Hormuz have effectively stalled for nearly seven weeks. August exports fell to roughly 220,000–255,000 barrels per day from about 2 million bpd in March, while renewed U.S.-Iran fighting pushed Brent back above USD 92 and intensified the global bond selloff.
items.whyItMatters: This is no longer only a risk premium: physical export impairment is reducing Iranian hard-currency inflows and extending the oil-to-inflation-to-rates channel. AGCI keeps 10–15% deployable liquidity, staggered duration and a moderate energy hedge rather than chasing spot oil.
items.agciSignal: PHYSICAL HORMUZ DISRUPTION / INFLATION TAIL RISK / KEEP LIQUIDITY

items.headline: Texas begins filtering speculative data-center grid demand, forcing a stricter AI infrastructure quality test
items.category: AI / Data Centers / Utilities / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Texas has halted or tightened new grid connections for data centers while authorities audit projects after power requests ballooned to levels far above plausible near-term demand. Similar financial and disclosure screens are emerging in other U.S. power markets.
items.whyItMatters: The AI infrastructure cycle remains structurally large, but connection queues and announced gigawatts cannot be treated as funded demand. AGCI raises the weight on deposits, contracted power, customer identity, financing, utilization and revenue visibility when underwriting data-center, utility and equipment exposure.
items.agciSignal: AI INFRASTRUCTURE / FILTER GHOST DEMAND / VERIFY CONTRACTED POWER AND FUNDING

items.headline: Euro-zone inflation rises above 3%, strengthening ECB rate-hike expectations
items.summary: Euro-zone inflation rose back above 3% in August, with energy costs contributing to the acceleration and markets increasing confidence that the ECB may need to tighten policy further.
items.whyItMatters: The inflation shock is becoming more global rather than purely U.S.-specific. Higher European policy expectations support a higher global discount-rate regime, pressure long-duration assets and reduce the probability that developed-market bonds rally together on growth weakness.
items.agciSignal: GLOBAL INFLATION BROADENING / HIGHER GLOBAL DISCOUNT RATE

items.newsletter: Review & Preview — See You in September / 31 Aug 2026
items.headline: August ended strong, but September seasonality coincides with elevated rates, oil risk and narrow AI leadership
items.summary: Barron's authorized newsletter highlights that major indexes completed a strong August but warns that September begins with a more difficult setup. The new Sept. 1 Barron's Daily also emphasizes Nvidia's increasingly complex circular ecosystem financing and a historically weaker seasonal window.
items.whyItMatters: Seasonality alone is not an investment signal, but it matters when valuation is already extreme and macro/geopolitical volatility is rising. AGCI does not reduce exposure mechanically for September; it raises the hurdle for adding beta and emphasizes breadth, cash flow and funded demand.
items.agciSignal: SEPTEMBER RISK WINDOW / DO NOT CHASE / QUALITY AND BREADTH FIRST

items.headline: SB Energy IPO filing tests whether public markets will fund AI infrastructure before operating proof
items.summary: SoftBank-backed SB Energy filed for a U.S. IPO after rapid revenue growth but large losses, with substantial data-center capacity planned and significant dependence on OpenAI and SoftBank-linked commitments.
items.whyItMatters: The filing is a useful market test for AI infrastructure financing. AGCI treats backlog and capacity announcements as lower-quality evidence than contracted cash flows, funded construction and diversified customers.
items.agciSignal: AI IPO TEST / BACKLOG IS NOT CASH FLOW / CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION
